proposal.hypothesis: The catalog has three distinct, valid SIMD-scan programs and no repeats, but none beat the 49.62 µs baseline: the 16-byte scan measured 60.43 µs, the selected lane-bisection parent 77.82 µs, and the 64-byte variant 81.00 µs. This contrasting SIMD-prefix/scalar-remainder hybrid tests whether repeatedly restarting SIMD scans and locating a lane after each decoded code point costs more than it saves. It skips only complete 16-byte ASCII vectors; on the first vector containing any high bit, it sends the suffix from that block boundary to the strict scalar decoder. This avoids assuming the high-bit byte is a lead and preserves bounded loads, but gives up SIMD scanning of later ASCII runs. Measure it on the official mixed-width n=65536 workload; do not infer a speedup from synthetic inputs.

retained: Replaced repeated SIMD scans interleaved with scalar code-point decoding with a bounded SIMD prefix scan over complete 16-byte blocks.

On the first vector with high-bit bytes, call the strict scalar validator on the suffix beginning at that vector's known code-point boundary; the scalar decoder validates any leading ASCII and treats the first high-bit byte as input to validate.
Retained scalar tail handling, UTF-8 validity rules, run ABI, output, and thread budget.
